topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture's historical context, core objectives, and connection to practical histopathology sessions.

topics.label: Discovery of tumor viruses, oncogenes, and transformation assays
topics.groupedBecause: They trace how the historical study of tumor viruses revealed cellular proto-oncogenes and led to experimental assays for cellular transformation.

topics.label: Classification and functional mechanisms of oncogenes and tumor suppressor genes
topics.groupedBecause: They define the classes of cancer-causing mutations and analyze how they alter cell cycle checkpoints and protein function.

topics.label: Mechanisms and cellular consequences of genetic instability
topics.groupedBecause: They examine how defects in DNA repair pathways, replication proofreading, and mitotic chromosome segregation generate sequence and chromosomal instability.

topics.label: Multistep tumor progression and hereditary cancer predisposition
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how the stepwise acquisition of sporadic and inherited genetic alterations drives tumor development and evolution.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and recommended reading
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture, offers recommended reading, and previews the next session on cancer hallmarks.
